WHAT'S CHANGED
Adobe Inc. (ADBE.O)FromTo
RatingEqual-weightUnderweight
Price Target$365.00$240.00

Adobe's concurrent freemium, leadership, and reinvestment transitions compound execution risk as GenAI disruption debate increasingly clouds the path to ARR reacceleration. At ~12X GAAP earnings, ample risk is likely priced in, but cleaner growth and AI monetization elsewhere support a relative UW.
Key Takeaways
Three concurrent transitions (freemium GTM, CEO/CFO transition, AI reinvestment) raise execution risk & further obscure path to ARR stabilization / acceleration
■ Best-in-class margins may be near peak as AI & low-ARPU engagement require more spend, leaving limited room for further operating leverage vs SaaS peers
Valuation at ~12x GAAP EPS likely prices in much risk, though limited visibility in timing / magnitude of a potential turnaround likely leave shares range-bound
- With durable ARR re-acceleration needed to assuage concerns on GenAI disruption risk in Creative Cloud, see shares as a relative UW near-term; reduce PT to $240
With this note, Adam Wood is assuming lead coverage of Adobe (ADBE) at Underweight rating and $240 PT.

Convergence of Transitions Lowers Visibility Into the Turnaround. Since moving to EW last fall (See Adobe Inc.: Haunted by What We Don't Know; Downgrade to Equal-weight), our thesis on Adobe was not that the company lacked urgency or innovation, but that the translation of that innovation into durable ARR acceleration had become increasingly difficult to underwrite as pools of Creative Cloud ARR became more exposed to GenAI substitution risk (and the relative difficulty in sizing this exposure across the base with any conviction). At the time, we highlighted that GenAI monetization was lagging initial expectations as Adobe largely prioritized ubiquity and adoption of products ahead of direct monetization. As such, divergence between ARR growth directionality and the pace of product innovation, rising usage,

and pricing benefit traversing the portfolio left investors questioning the path to reacceleration. Since then, three incremental transitions have become more apparent to us (and the market broadly) that further complicate that path – a more explicit freemium route-to-market pivot, a simultaneous CEO/CFO leadership transition, and an operating model shift from margin harvesting toward AI reinvestment. While each transition may be manageable in isolation, their convergence raises the bar for execution at a time when other areas of Software offer cleaner evidence of growth durability, operating leverage, and / or near-term AI monetization. In addition, in our assessment of our broader coverage 'Moat and Journey' scores as it relates to AI readiness, Adobe screens relatively weaker across SaaS (described in detail below). Net, while we acknowledge that shares trading at ~12x CY27 GAAP P/E price in much of this disruption risk, Adobe's simultaneous transitions reduce visibility – and therefore our conviction – in the timing and magnitude of a potential turnaround. We expect this uncertainty and execution risk to remain an overhang on investor willingness to engage with shares, keeping the multiple depressed and range-bound, supporting our relative UW view (Exhibit 1).
Exhibit 1: ADBE Shares Trade at the Low End of the Mature at Scale Software Peer Group
Source: Company Data, MS

Moat and Journey Framework. In our Sector Insight today, we evaluated our software coverage universe through the lens of the opportunity and threat from AI. We looked at companies across two dimensions: the Moat a company has against AI-native entrants and increasingly easier code creation, and the Journey a company must take as it adapts to the pricing model, development cycle, and interaction method that will define the next phase of software. Adobe screens in the middle of the pack overall (3rd quintile, with a 64/100 overall score) with a Moat score of 33/50 set against a Journey score of 31/50 (Exhibit 2). On Moat, we see Adobe's risk less in brand, distribution, or domain expertise, where its installed base, creative professional standardization, and decades of workflow-specific product depth remain meaningful advantages. Rather, risks concentrate in lower workflow criticality and weaker system-of-record characteristics relative to other software franchises – Adobe remains deeply embedded in creative workflows, but portions of the workflow are task-based, promptable, and increasingly exposed to AI-native substitution, particularly where users are not anchored in enterprise approvals, compliance, or broader content supply-chain orchestration. On Journey, we see
MS | RESEARCH
IDEA

Adobe's strengths most squarely in its scale, strong profitability, balance-sheet capacity, and thus, its ability to reinvest aggressively in both organic and inorganic innovation. However, this investment intensity has not yet translated into a visible growth inflection, leaving investors to underwrite AI as both an opportunity and a disruption risk in Creative. Thus, we could get more constructive on Adobe's Journey with evidence that rising AI usage and freemium traffic are sustainably converting into paid ARR, ultimately driving sustained and / or accelerating ARR growth towards the low teens.
Exhibit 2: Adobe Positioned at the Middle of the Pack on Both Moat and Journey
Source: MS
Along with Adobe's relative position in our Moat & Journey framework analysis, we downgrade to UW on the culmination of three impending transitions creating heightened execution risk:

1. Freemium Acquisition and Monetization Transition Stifles ARR Visibility. At Adobe's 2Q print, the company effectively lowered organic ARR growth (by ~$500M) as full year ARR growth guidance (+10.2% YoY, reflecting a trend of continued deceleration from ~11.5% in FY25, Exhibit 3) was maintained despite the closure of the Semrush acquisition. This outlook reflects the strategic choice to accelerate freemium MAU growth and defer previously planned Creative Cloud pricing action, with management framing the ARR impact as split roughly evenly between those two drivers. Management commentary suggested the freemium pivot is in response to AI pulling demand away from traditional branded purchase journeys and toward intent-based creative tasks. While this dynamic does appear to be showing up in traffic patterns (Business Professional & Consumer traffic on Adobe.com was up 35% YoY as of 2Q, and creative freemium MAUs increased from 50M to 90M YoY), management is increasingly routing that demand into Acrobat, Express, and Firefly experiences rather than direct-to-paid funnels. Accordingly, we see a near-term Creative growth inflection incrementally more difficult to underwrite. While freemium can be the correct long-term strategy (especially if the alternative is pushing high-intent traffic into a paid flow too early and losing the user), monetization is unlikely to be linear. Adobe now has to scale and optimize its existing conversion infrastructure – including paywall timing, credit consumption and upsell journeys – across a much larger creative freemium audience without undermining engagement, and that process can take time. As such, we could see ARR growth continuing to decelerate into FY27 absent a more aggressive than

Exhibit 3: Total ARR Growth Continues To Decelerate
Source: Company Data, MS

2. 'Margin Transition' as Adobe Reinvests in Organic Innovation + Leans into Strategic M&A. With best in class margins across SaaS (Exhibit 4), Adobe has meaningful room to invest in order to participate in this innovation cycle. However, even after stepping up investments through FY25, particularly as it relates to R&D (Exhibit 5), Adobe still ranks atop our efficiency analysis (Exhibit 6 & Exhibit 7), suggesting that the company may be approaching peak efficiency, presenting less leverage opportunity on a go forward basis. Thus, we could actually see some downside bias to margins in the near term as: 1) the freemium shift effectively pulls more engagement (investment) into low ARPU cohorts ahead of monetization (return on investment); and 2) ramping AI usage could weigh on gross margins as the company prioritizes optimizing brand and customer loyalty over near-term monetization. With operating profit per employee already optimized, margins already near peak, and management still needing to invest organically and inorganically to defend Creative, we see less opportunity for a standard efficiency cycle to drive material margin upside. To create a step-function in profitability from here, Adobe would likely need a meaningful restructuring – a difficult message to square while currently needing to execute against a strategy that depends on accelerating innovation, improving freemium conversion, and proving AI can expand rather than cannibalize the Creative base.

3. Timing of Leadership Transition Compounds Strategic Risk. The CEO and CFO transitions do not necessarily change our view of Adobe's product depth, but they undoubtedly raise the execution hurdle at a difficult point in the narrative. On 1Q26 earnings, long-time CEO Shantanu Narayen announced he will transition from CEO once a successor is appointed while remaining Chair, with the Board evaluating internal and external candidates. Separately, CFO Dan Durn announced his departure (to Marvell) concurrent with 2Q26 earnings, with Steve Day appointed as
MS | RESEARCH
IDEA

interim CFO. In our view, a planned succession would be manageable in a steadier period, but this is occurring as Adobe is rewiring go-to-market around freemium, deferring Creative Cloud pricing, integrating acquisitions, and most crucially, asking investors to underwrite a delayed monetization curve as it pushes more aggressively towards a freemium model. Until the new leadership team has set priorities and the market can assess whether the freemium / AI reinvestment cycle converts into ARR acceleration, we expect 'show me' sentiment to persist.

PT to $240. We lower our price target to $240 (from $365 previously) as we now apply a 9x multiple (vs. 13x previously, still a discount to Adobe's historical average) to our FY27 earnings/share estimate of ~$27.23. This results in our $240 price target, which implies ~0.6x PEG (discount to SaaS peers). Our price target also implies ~12x CY27 GAAP P/E, also a modest discount to SaaS peers, which we see as warranted given outsized GenAI disruption debate and heightened near-term execution concerns.

Risks to Our UW Call: 1) Faster than anticipated conversion of freemium traffic; 2) new CEO / CFO meaningfully inflecting profitability through strategic restructuring; and 3) AI proving net-expansive to the Creative franchise, with Firefly / Express adoption, AI credit monetization, and enterprise content supply-chain demand driving a durable ARR reacceleration and alleviating Creative Cloud disruption concerns.

UNDERWEIGHT THESIS

■ Adobe retains a strong moat in pro creative workflows & enterprise content supply chains, supported by its brand, distribution & workflow-specific product depth. However, consumers, business users & simpler marketers remain vulnerable to AI-native substitution

■ Convergence of freemium, leadership & reinvestment transitions raise execution risk as deferred CC pricing, uncertain freemium conversion & simultaneous CEO/CFO transitions reduce visibility into ARR growth re-accel

■ Best-in-class margins provide capacity to defend franchise, but see limited incremental leverage optionality. ~10x GAAP P/E discounts risk, though see cleaner growth, leverage & AI monetization oppty elsewhere. Relative UW

Effective conversion of freemium traffic expands the user base and pushes pricing higher, supporting a total revenue CAGR of 12%. Operating margin of ~45% results in FY27 EPS of $28.20. ADBE trades at 12x EPS, largely inline with mature scaled Software peers, supported by a mid-teens% EPS CAGR, yielding $340/share.
BASE CASE
$240.00 BEAR CASE
9x Base Case 2027e EPS of $27.23

Total revenue grows at 10% CAGR from FY24-FY27. Operating margin of 44.7% results in FY27 EPS of $27.23 and a FY24-FY27 EPS CAGR of 14%. At a 9x EPS multiple in FY27e, yielding $240/share, ADBE trades at ~0.6x PEG, a discount to its historical average.
6x Bear Case 2027e EPS of $26.32

Competition from Al-natives limits ability to effectively convert freemium traffic to paid ARR, driving further growth deceleration. Margins remain ~45% in FY27 as growth investments moderate, resulting in FY27e EPS of $26.32. The stock trades at 6x FY27e EPS, which yields $160/share.
